los.text: Obtain a 12-lead ECG recording and ensure correct electrode placement.
los.html:
ElectrodePosition
V14th intercostal space, right sternal edge
V24th intercostal space, left sternal edge
V3Midway between V2 and V4
V45th intercostal space, midclavicular line
V5Anterior axillary line, level with V4
V6Midaxillary line, level with V4
Limb leadsRed: right arm, yellow: left arm, green: left leg, black: right leg ("Ride Your Green Bike")
1Identity, explain, consent, privacy; patient lying at 45°, relaxed, still.
2Clean/shave/dry the skin; apply electrodes in the correct positions (under the breast for V4–V6 in women).
3Check the machine settings: 25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV, filter.
4
  • Record
  • Check quality (no artefact, no lead reversal: e.g. negative lead I)
  • Label with name, date, time, symptoms
  • Show a doctor if abnormal.

los.text: Perform a peripheral arterial and vascular examination systematically and accurately.
los.html:
StepDetail
Inspect legs
  • Colour (pallor, cyanosis, rubor)
  • Hair loss
  • Shiny skin
  • Ulcers (arterial: punched out, toes/heels, painful; venous: gaiter area, shallow)
  • Gangrene
  • Scars
  • Varicose veins
  • Oedema
FeelTemperature gradient, capillary refill
Pulses (both sides)
  • Femoral (midinguinal point), popliteal (knee flexed, deep), posterior tibial (behind medial malleolus), dorsalis pedis (lateral to EHL)
  • Also radial, carotid, abdominal aorta (expansile?)
AuscultateFemoral and carotid bruits, aorta
Buerger's testRaise the legs: pallor at <20° = severe ischaemia; then dangle: reactive hyperaemia (rubor)
NeurologySensation (diabetic neuropathy)
  • Finish: ABPI (≥0.9 normal; <0.9 PAD; <0.5 severe/critical; >1.3 calcified), duplex ultrasound, cardiovascular risk factors.

los.text: Recognise common Cardiology symptoms and interpret a number of clinical cases.
los.html:
SymptomKey cardiac questions
Chest painCharacter (crushing vs pleuritic vs tearing), exertional, radiation, sweating, duration, relief with rest/GTN
BreathlessnessExertional, orthopnoea, PND, ankle swelling
PalpitationsFast/slow, regular/irregular, onset and offset, triggers, syncope
SyncopeExertional (structural), warning, recovery, injuries
ClaudicationCalf pain on walking relieved by rest, walking distance
Example caseInterpretation
Central crushing chest pain + ST elevation V1–V4Anterior STEMI → primary PCI
Exertional chest tightness relieved by rest, normal ECGStable angina
Breathlessness, raised JVP, oedema, high BNPHeart failure → echo
Irregular palpitations, irregularly irregular ECGAF → rate control, CHA₂DS₂-VASc

los.text: Perform a competent upper limb neurological examination with increased confidence.
los.html:
• Upper limb neurology (session title: lower limb): see ICM Year 1 › Neurology & cognition › LOs 1
    • 2 and 3 for the upper limb routine
    • and ICM Year 1 › Neurology & cognition › LO 6 for the lower limb. "Increased confidence": fluent sequence
    • MRC grading
    • reinforcement
    • mapping to root vs nerve
    • clear presentation.
